commands.review_summary:
Updates Slack Socket Mode startup status to remain connected but report degraded health and an identity error when authentication fails or bot identity is unavailable, with focused helper tests.

PR surface: Source +31, Tests +54. Total +85 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: current main unconditionally publishes healthy status when Socket Mode starts, while the existing authentication path can leave bot identity unavailable. The contributor also reproduced the relevant Slack API response shapes, but not the complete patched runtime path.

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). Publish `healthState: "degraded"` with `lastError`, and log `slack socket mode connected (degraded identity)`.

## User Impact

- Misconfigured bot tokens / failed `auth.test` no longer look healthy in channel status.
- Valid bot-token installs stay `healthy` on connect.
- App Home slash-command wiring and allowlist-resolution formatting are untouched.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `204aa27fa823936f88ba69da6fb20d9491165976` (rebased onto current `main`)

### Rank-up coverage

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Rebase onto current main | done |
| Provider-path coverage: `user_id` without `bot_id` → degraded | unit test + live Scenario B |
| Redacted real Slack API / status-path output for healthy-bot, user-token, auth.test-failure | live transcript below |
| No App Home / resolution-format churn | compare view is 3 files, status-only |

### L1 unit (provider-path)

- `marks socket mode degraded when boot identity is unavailable`
- `marks socket mode degraded for user_id without bot_id (bot-gated contract)` — mirrors `monitorSlackProvider` auth handling + `formatSlackBotTokenIdentityWarning` + `publishSlackConnectedStatus(..., { degraded: true })`

Local Vitest in this contributor workspace hit an unrelated `openclaw/plugin-sdk/approval-reference-runtime` resolve failure; CI extension checks are the green gate for this head.

### L3 live Slack API call logs (redacted) — 2026-07-13

Used live Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-…`) and User OAuth Token (`xoxp-…`) from local env only (not committed). **Rotate these tokens — they were pasted into chat.**

Public/private channel IDs exercised via `conversations.info` (ids redacted below). Full Socket Mode `apps.connections.open` needs App-Level Token `xapp-…` (not provided); proof covers live `auth.test` + channel API + the exact provider identity → `setStatus` / runtime log contract that `onStarted` now calls.

### Before / after contract

| Case | Live `auth.test` | BEFORE (`main` onStarted) | AFTER (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valid `xoxb` (has `bot_id`) | ok + bot_id | `healthState: healthy` | `healthState: healthy` + log `slack socket mode connected` |
| `xoxp` as botToken (`user_id`, no `bot_id`) | ok, no bot_id | still `healthy` (bug) | `healthState: degraded` + `lastError` warning + log `… (degraded identity)` |
| Invalid token | `invalid_auth` | still `healthy` (bug) | `healthState: degraded` + `lastError: invalid_auth` |

- `extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.ts` — `identityDegraded` gate on Socket `onStarted`
- `extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.reconnect.test.ts` — healthy / missing-identity / user-without-bot_id coverage
